note_on_commit_hash: Brief mentioned 4d18bf1 but actual T5 commit is 6de72db (feat: task 5 — CLI commands). Reviewed 6de72db.
summary: All four spec-required TDD anchors are present and correctly drive their underlying decisions. Test isolation via MNEMONIC_CONFIG_DIR + tmpdir is clean throughout (every suite uses withTmpConfigDir/cleanup). Network is mocked exclusively via vi.fn-wrapped globalThis.fetch — no real network calls. Lines coverage 77.63% clears the spec-mandated 75% gate. Major gaps: zero 5xx server-error tests on any happy-path command, malformed-JWT tested only for alg=none, and the login interactive anchor relies on Server.prototype.listen monkey-patching (correctly self-flagged in decisions.md). Branch coverage 68.14% is below a typical 80% bar but the spec only sets a lines gate for CLI, so this is acceptable per spec — flagging for round 2 follow-up not blocking.

concerns_round_2.topic: 5xx server-error coverage missing across all server-calling commands
concerns_round_2.ask: Add at least one 'returns ServerError (exit 2) on 5xx' test per command. The spec defines errors.ts::ServerError with exitCode=2 and tech-spec calls out fault-injection toggles including '5xx-on-token-exchange'. Without these tests, a regression that swallows 5xx as UserError would not be caught.
concerns_round_2.suggested_minimal_addition: 5 tests (one per command + login token exchange 5xx). Reuse existing fetchMock pattern; switch status to 500/503 and assert ServerError instance with exitCode 2.

concerns_round_2.topic: Server.prototype.listen monkey-patch is brittle (already self-flagged in decisions.md concern #5)
concerns_round_2.ask: Refactor login.ts to accept an injectable HTTP server factory (DI) — e.g. `runLogin({ httpFactory?: typeof http.createServer })`. Test then passes a fake factory that returns a mock server, eliminating the prototype patch. Recommended for round 2 but not blocking — the current test does work and decisions.md acknowledges the trade-off (frozen ESM exports prevent vi.spyOn on http.createServer).
concerns_round_2.alternative_if_DI_too_invasive: Accept the patch as-is and add a defensive try/finally restore even if the test throws synchronously (current code already has finally — check this is bullet-proof under expect-rejects path).

concerns_round_2.topic: Malformed JWT coverage is thin (only alg=none)
concerns_round_2.ask: Add 3-4 cases: (a) JWT with missing exp, (b) JWT with non-string sub, (c) JWT with alg=RS256 (spec requires HS256), (d) JWT with malformed base64 in any segment. All should produce AuthError exit 4.

concerns_round_2.topic: bin/mnemonic.ts 61% line coverage — auto-run guard path uncovered
concerns_round_2.ask: Acceptable to leave uncovered. The auto-run guard (`if (invokedDirectly) parseAsync(process.argv)`) and per-command `.action()` closures are integration-shape code; testing them requires execa subprocess invocation which spec explicitly allowed avoiding. Recommend a single execa-driven smoke test (1-2 invocations: `--version` and `init --force`) to lift bin coverage to ~85% and serve as a deployment regression guard. NOT a blocker — current 61% is justified.

Self-flagged in decisions.md as concerns #1 and #3. Hot misses are renderer (TTY-only) branches and login.ts::awaitCallback error paths (405/404/missing-code). Tech-spec line 323 only sets a CLI lines gate (≥75%), so this passes spec literally. Recommend a focused login error-callback test in round 2 that POSTs each shape (405, 404, missing-state, error_description) and observes AuthError. Lifts branches to ~78% without new infrastructure.
concerns_round_2.decision: acceptable per spec — flag for follow-up

concerns_round_2.ask: Acceptable. The TDD anchor explicitly asserts default whoami calls fetch ZERO times (Decision 14). Adding a --with-count test would be supplementary, not regression-protecting, since the path reuses recall.test.ts's tested machinery. Skip unless --with-count becomes default in a future iteration.
